body.en: Mechanics begins with motion in a straight line under constant acceleration.
For constant acceleration: \( v=u+at \), \( s=ut+\tfrac12 at^{2} \), \( v^{2}=u^{2}+2as \). Velocity is the derivative of displacement; acceleration the derivative of velocity.

Proportional Invariance, Linear Structure & Quantitative Modeling: Across Cambridge International AS Level (9709 Paper 1 / Paper 4 / Paper 5), multi-step problems reduce to identifying invariant quantities—constant rates of change \(m = \dfrac{\Delta y}{\Delta x}\), conservation of total work/mass, or linear system rank conditions. A two-variable linear system \(a_1 x + b_1 y = c_1\), \(a_2 x + b_2 y = c_2\) has a unique intersection if \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} \ne \dfrac{b_1}{b_2}\), no solution (parallel lines) if \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{b_1}{b_2} \ne \dfrac{c_1}{c_2}\), and infinitely many solutions if all three ratios coincide.

body.en:
SUVAT vs Calculus: SUVAT formulas apply ONLY when acceleration is constant. If velocity or acceleration varies with time (e.g. \(v = 3t^2 - 12t\)), SUVAT yields zero marks — you must differentiate (\(a = \frac{dv}{dt}\)) or integrate (\(s = \int v\,dt\)).

Velocity-Time graphs: Gradient equals acceleration (\(a = \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t}\)). Total area under the graph equals displacement. For distance vs displacement: if the graph drops below the time axis (negative velocity), distance sums the absolute areas, whereas displacement nets them.

Vertical motion sign convention: Fix a reference direction at the start (usually upwards positive). Under this convention, acceleration is \(a = -g = -9.8\text{ m/s}^2\) (or \(-9.81\)). Any position below the launch point corresponds to negative displacement \(s < 0\).

Why Successive Multipliers & Harmonic Average Speed Work: If a quantity \(Q_0\) undergoes a percentage change \(p\%\) followed by \(q\%\), the compound multiplier is the product of individual scale factors:

\[ Q_{\text{final}} = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p}{100}\right)\!\left(1 + \frac{q}{100}\right) = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p + q}{100} + \frac{pq}{10000}\right) \]

Notice the cross term \(\dfrac{pq}{10000}\): an increase of \(p\%\) followed by a decrease of \(p\%\) yields \(Q_0\bigl(1 - (p/100)^2\bigr) < Q_0\). Similarly, traveling equal distance \(d\) at speeds \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) takes total time \(T = \frac{d}{v_1} + \frac{d}{v_2}\), so average speed is the harmonic mean \(v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{2d}{d/v_1 + d/v_2} = \dfrac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).

problem.en: A particle moves so that its velocity at time \(t\) s is \(v=3t^2-12t+9\) m/s. Find (a) the acceleration at \(t=2\), (b) when the particle is momentarily at rest.

solution.en:
(a) \(a=\dfrac{dv}{dt}=6t-12\). At \(t=2\): \(a=0\) m/s².

(b) \(v=0\Rightarrow3(t-1)(t-3)=0\Rightarrow t=1\) s or \(t=3\) s.

problem.en: A particle's velocity \( v \) m/s at time \( t \) seconds is given by \( v = \frac{1}{2}t^2 - 3t + 5 \). The displacement of the particle from a fixed origin is \( s \) metres. It is known that at \( t = 2 \), the displacement \( s = 7 \). The displacement function \( s(t) \) can be expressed in the form \( s(t) = At^3 + Bt^2 + Ct + D \). Find the value of \( A \) and the value of \( D \).

solution.en: We are given the velocity function \( v(t) = \frac{1}{2}t^2 - 3t + 5 \). Since displacement \( s \) is the integral of velocity with respect to time, we have: \[ s(t) = \int v(t) \, dt = \int \left( \frac{1}{2}t^2 - 3t + 5 \right) dt \] Integrating term by term, we get: \[ s(t) = \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{t^3}{3} - 3 \cdot \frac{t^2}{2} + 5t + K \] \[ s(t) = \frac{1}{6}t^3 - \frac{3}{2}t^2 + 5t + K \] Comparing this with the given form \( s(t) = At^3 + Bt^2 + Ct + D \), we can identify \( A = \frac{1}{6} \), \( B = -\frac{3}{2} \), \( C = 5 \). The constant of integration is \( K = D \). We are given that at \( t = 2 \), \( s = 7 \). We can use this information to find the value of \( D \): \[ 7 = \frac{1}{6}(2)^3 - \frac{3}{2}(2)^2 + 5(2) + D \] \[ 7 = \frac{1}{6}(8) - \frac{3}{2}(4) + 10 + D \] \[ 7 = \frac{8}{6} - \frac{12}{2} + 10 + D \] \[ 7 = \frac{4}{3} - 6 + 10 + D \] \[ 7 = \frac{4}{3} + 4 + D \] Subtracting 4 from both sides: \[ 3 = \frac{4}{3} + D \] To find \( D \), subtract \( \frac{4}{3} \) from 3: \[ D = 3 - \frac{4}{3} = \frac{9}{3} - \frac{4}{3} = \frac{5}{3} \] Therefore, \( A = \frac{1}{6} \) and \( D = \frac{5}{3} \).

problem.en: A particle moves along a straight line. Its velocity, \( v \) m/s, at time \( t \) seconds is given by \( v = 3t - 2 \). Find the displacement of the particle during the first 4 seconds of its motion.

solution.en: The displacement of the particle can be found by integrating the velocity function with respect to time. The displacement \( s \) is given by: \[ s = \int v \, dt \] In this case, \( v = 3t - 2 \). \[ s = \int (3t - 2) \, dt \] Integrating, we get: \[ s = \frac{3}{2}t^2 - 2t + C \] To find the displacement during the first 4 seconds, we evaluate the definite integral from \( t=0 \) to \( t=4 \). We can assume \( C=0 \) for calculating the change in displacement from \( t=0 \). \[ s(4) - s(0) = \left[ \frac{3}{2}t^2 - 2t \right]_0^4 \] \[ s(4) - s(0) = \left( \frac{3}{2}(4)^2 - 2(4) \right) - \left( \frac{3}{2}(0)^2 - 2(0) \right) \] \[ s(4) - s(0) = \left( \frac{3}{2}(16) - 8 \right) - (0) \] \[ s(4) - s(0) = (3 \times 8 - 8) \] \[ s(4) - s(0) = (24 - 8) \] \[ s(4) - s(0) = 16 \] Therefore, the displacement of the particle during the first 4 seconds is 16 m.

question.en: A train accelerates uniformly from rest to \(30\text{ m/s}\) in \(20\text{ s}\), travels at constant speed \(30\text{ m/s}\) for \(60\text{ s}\), and then decelerates uniformly to rest in \(15\text{ s}\). Find: (a) the acceleration in the first phase, (b) the total distance travelled, (c) the average speed for the entire journey.

solution.en:
(a) \(a_1 = \dfrac{v - u}{t} = \dfrac{30 - 0}{20} = 1.5\text{ m/s}^2\).
(b) Total distance is the area of the trapezoid on the \(v\)-\(t\) graph with parallel sides \(60\text{ s}\) and \(20 + 60 + 15 = 95\text{ s}\), and height \(30\text{ m/s}\): \[s = \dfrac{60 + 95}{2} \times 30 = \dfrac{155}{2} \times 30 = 155 \times 15 = 2325\text{ m}\] (c) Average speed: \[\text{Average speed} = \dfrac{\text{Total distance}}{\text{Total time}} = \dfrac{2325\text{ m}}{95\text{ s}} \approx 24.47\text{ m/s} \approx 24.5\text{ m/s (3 s.f.)}\]

hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(a_1 = \dfrac{v - u}{t} = \dfrac{30 - 0}{20} = 1.5\text{ m/s}^2\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: (b) Total distance is the area of the trapezoid on the \(v\)-\(t\) graph with parallel sides \(60\text{ s}\) and \(20 + 60 + 15 = 95\text{ s}\), and height \(30\text{ m/s}\): \(s = \dfrac{60 + 95}{2} \times 30 = \dfrac{155}{2} \times 30 = 155 \times 15\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(v\) ، \(t\) ، \(60\text{ s}\) ، \(20 + 60 + 15 = 95\text{ s}\) ، \(30\text{ m/s}\) ، \(s = \dfrac{60 + 95}{2} \times 30 = \dfrac{155}{2} \times 30 = 155 \times 15\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: (c) Average speed: \(\text{Average speed} = \dfrac{\text{Total distance}}{\text{Total time}} = \dfrac{2325\text{ m}}{95\text{ s}} \approx 24.47\text{ m/s} \approx 24.5\text{ m/s (3 s.f.)}\).

question.en: A stone is thrown vertically upwards with speed \(15\text{ m/s}\) from the top of a cliff \(40\text{ m}\) above sea level. Taking \(g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2\) and upwards as positive: (a) find the maximum height reached above the cliff, (b) calculate the time taken for the stone to reach the sea.

solution.en: (a) At maximum height, \(v = 0\). \(u = +15\text{ m/s}\), \(a = -9.8\text{ m/s}^2\): \[v^2 = u^2 + 2as \Rightarrow 0 = 15^2 + 2(-9.8)s \Rightarrow 19.6s = 225 \Rightarrow s = \dfrac{225}{19.6} \approx 11.48\text{ m} \approx 11.5\text{ m}\] (b) At the sea, the displacement relative to the launch point is \(s = -40\text{ m}\). Use \(s = ut + \tfrac{1}{2}at^2\): \[-40 = 15t + \tfrac{1}{2}(-9.8)t^2 \Rightarrow -40 = 15t - 4.9t^2 \Rightarrow 4.9t^2 - 15t - 40 = 0\] Solve via quadratic formula: \[t = \dfrac{15 \pm \sqrt{(-15)^2 - 4(4.9)(-40)}}{2(4.9)} = \dfrac{15 \pm \sqrt{225 + 784}}{9.8} = \dfrac{15 \pm \sqrt{1009}}{9.8}\] Since \(\sqrt{1009} \approx 31.765\), and \(t > 0\): \[t = \dfrac{15 + 31.765}{9.8} = \dfrac{46.765}{9.8} \approx 4.77\text{ s (3 s.f.)}\]

hints.en: (a) At maximum height, \(v = 0\). \(u = +15\text{ m/s}\), \(a = -9.8\text{ m/s}^2\): \(v^2 = u^2 + 2as \Rightarrow 0 = 15^2 + 2(-9.8)s \Rightarrow 19.6s = 225 \Rightarrow s = \dfrac{225}{19.6} = 11.48\text{ m}\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(v = 0\) ، \(u = +15\text{ m/s}\) ، \(a = -9.8\text{ m/s}^2\) ، \(v^2 = u^2 + 2as \Rightarrow 0 = 15^2 + 2(-9.8)s \Rightarrow 19.6s = 225 \Rightarrow s = \dfrac{225}{19.6} = 11.48\text{ m}\) لتبسيط الخطوة.
تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(\sqrt{1009} \approx 31.765\) ، \(t > 0\) ، \(t = \dfrac{15 + 31.765}{9.8} = \dfrac{46.765}{9.8}\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

question.en:
[Practice 3 · Medium] A particle moves in a straight line such that its displacement \(s\) metres from a fixed origin after \(t\) seconds is given by the equation \(s = t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t + 2\).

The velocity of the particle is given by \(v = \frac{ds}{dt}\).

Find the value of \(t\) for which the particle is instantaneously at rest and then determine the displacement of the particle at that instant.

hints.en: The displacement is given by \(s = t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t + 2\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(s = t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t + 2\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: To find the velocity, we differentiate the displacement with respect to time: \(v = \frac{ds}{dt} = \frac{d}{dt}(t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t + 2) = 3t^2 - 12t + 9\). The particle is instantaneously at rest when its velocity is zero, i.e., \(v=0\).
The question implies finding *a* value of t and the corresponding displacement.

solution.en:
The displacement is given by \(s = t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t + 2\).
Differentiate with respect to time to find the velocity:
\(v = \frac{ds}{dt} = 3t^2 - 12t + 9\).

The particle is instantaneously at rest when \(v = 0\):
\(3t^2 - 12t + 9 = 0 \implies t^2 - 4t + 3 = 0 \implies (t-1)(t-3) = 0\), giving \(t = 1\text{ s}\) or \(t = 3\text{ s}\).

At \(t = 1\text{ s}\): \(s = 1^3 - 6(1)^2 + 9(1) + 2 = 6\text{ m}\).
At \(t = 3\text{ s}\): \(s = 3^3 - 6(3)^2 + 9(3) + 2 = 2\text{ m}\).

question.en: [Practice 4 · Hard] A particle starts from the origin \(O\) with initial velocity \(5\text{ m s}^{-1}\) and moves along a straight line with acceleration \(a = 6t - 4\text{ m s}^{-2}\) at time \(t\text{ s}\). Find its displacement from \(O\) when \(t = 3\text{ s}\).
question.ar: [تدريب 4 · صعب] ينطلق جسيم من نقطة الأصل \(O\) بسرعة ابتدائية \(5\text{ m s}^{-1}\) ويتحرك في خط مستقيم بتسارع \(a = 6t - 4\text{ m s}^{-2}\) عند الزمن \(t\text{ s}\). أوجد إزاحته عن \(O\) عندما \(t = 3\text{ s}\).

hints.en: Integrate \(a = 6t - 4\) with respect to \(t\) and use \(v(0) = 5\) to find the velocity function \(v(t)\).
hints.ar: كامل \(a = 6t - 4\) بالنسبة إلى \(t\) واستعمل \(v(0) = 5\) لإيجاد دالة السرعة \(v(t)\).

hints.en: Obtain \(v(t) = 3t^2 - 4t + 5\), then integrate again with \(s(0) = 0\) to obtain \(s(t)\).
hints.ar: تحصل على \(v(t) = 3t^2 - 4t + 5\)، ثم كامل مجدداً مع \(s(0) = 0\) لإيجاد \(s(t)\).

solution.en:
Integrating acceleration gives \(v(t) = \int (6t - 4)\,\mathrm{d}t = 3t^2 - 4t + C_1\). Using \(v(0) = 5\), \(C_1 = 5\), so \(v(t) = 3t^2 - 4t + 5\).

Integrating velocity with \(s(0) = 0\) gives \(s(t) = t^3 - 2t^2 + 5t\).

At \(t = 3\), \(s(3) = 27 - 18 + 15 = 24\text{ m}\).
solution.ar:
بتكامل التسارع نجد \(v(t) = 3t^2 - 4t + C_1\)، وبما أن \(v(0) = 5\) فإن \(C_1 = 5\).

بتكامل السرعة مع \(s(0) = 0\) نجد \(s(t) = t^3 - 2t^2 + 5t\).

عند \(t = 3\): \(s(3) = 27 - 18 + 15 = 24\text{ m}\).

question.en: [Practice 5 · Medium] A cyclist passes point \(A\) at \(12\text{ m s}^{-1}\) and decelerates uniformly at \(1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}\) until coming to rest at point \(B\). Find the distance \(AB\) and the time taken.
question.ar: [تدريب 5 · متوسط] يمر راكب دراجة بالنقطة \(A\) بسرعة \(12\text{ m s}^{-1}\) ويتباطأ بانتظام بمعدل \(1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}\) حتى يتوقف عند النقطة \(B\). أوجد المسافة \(AB\) والزمن المستغرق.

hints.ar: اكتب معطيات الحركة المنتظمة: \(u = 12\) و\(v = 0\) و\(a = -1.5\).

hints.en: Use \(v^2 = u^2 + 2as\) to find the stopping distance \(s\).
hints.ar: استعمل العلاقة \(v^2 = u^2 + 2as\) لإيجاد مسافة التوقف \(s\).

hints.en: Use \(v = u + at\) to solve for the stopping time \(t\).
hints.ar: استعمل \(v = u + at\) لحساب زمن التوقف \(t\).
